Title: Full potential linearized augmented plane wave calculations of structuraland electronic properties of BN, BP, BAs and BSb
Authors: A Zaoui, F El Haj Hassan
Description: A theoretical study of structural and electronic properties of boron compounds BN, BP, BAs and BSb is presented, using the full potential linearized augmented plane wave method. In this approach, the generalized gradient approximation was used for the exchange-correlation potential. Ground state properties such as lattice parameter, bulk modulus and its pressure derivative are calculated as well as structural transition pressure. The band structure is obtained for both zincblende and rocksalt structures. We also give the valence charge density at equilibrium lattice constant and at transition pressure. We show from the latter quantity the inverse role between cation and anion for BP, BAs and BSb. Results are discussed and compared with experimental and other theoretical data with reasonable agreement.

Description: The structural, electronic and thermodynamic properties of the SrS1–xOx ternary mixed crystals have been studied using the ab initio full potential linearized augmented plane wave (FP-LAPW) method within density functional theory. The effect of composition on lattice parameter, bulk modulus and band gap was investigated. The lattice constants from Vegard's law and the bulk modulus from linear concentration dependence were observed for the alloys. The microscopic origins of the gap bowing were explained by using the approach of Zunger and co-workers. The thermodynamic stability of these alloys was investigated by calculating the excess enthalpy of mixing ΔHm as well as the phase diagram. In addition to FP-LAPW method, the composition dependence of the refractive index and the dielectric constant was studied by different models.

Description: The prototype materials of the family Cu-In/Ga-Se of the chalcopyrite structure are CuInSe2 and CuGaSe2. They are since long under study, by both experimental and theoretical techniques. They are known to possess unique properties in what regards their radiation stability, to the point that the easily created radiation defects do not deteriorate the photovoltaic efficiency. These materials are very prone to build intermediate phases, known as ordered-defect phases, and to create a variety of internal structural defects: vacancies, interstitials, anti-sites. The structural phase diagram in the Cu-In-Se triangle is quite rich. The quality of samples used for experimental studies varies, and the problems of reliable structural identification are common. Through this work we are going to represent the structural and electronic properties of the both crystals using first principle full potential-linearized augmented plane wave (FP-LAPW) plus local orbital method within the density funtional theory (DFT). The structural properties at equilibrium are investegated by using the new form of generalized gradiant approximation (GGA_PBEsol) that are based on the optimization of total energy. For band structure calculations, both GGA and modified Becke-Johnson (mBJ) of the exchange correlation energy and potential, respectively, are used.
